articles.title: Another Blonde Ole Miss Fan Goes Viral Moments Before Trinidad Chambliss Touchdown
articles.summary: Crowd shots do not seem to stop going viral on social media during Ole Miss game days. An ABC cameraman panned to a fan in the stands early in the fourth qua...
articles.body:
Crowd shots do not seem to stop going viral on social media during Ole Miss game days. An ABC cameraman panned to a fan in the stands early in the fourth quarter against Auburn, and the clip was circulating fast before the Rebels finished a 45-15 win. It landed two plays before Trinidad Chambliss threw a touchdown.

This is becoming a pattern for Ole Miss games. Sara Smith went viral in the September 6 opener against Louisville, holding her phone overhead as the Cardinals scored. Three weeks later, an ABC cameraman drew accusations of lingering on a fan in the stands during Florida's 52-28 win.

"The cameraman doing his job and finding the most attractive white blonde for the nation to see on national TV during the Ole Miss vs Auburn game," An X handle by the name MAGA Elvis captioned a video on X . The video showed a fan in a light-blue top waving a rag with one arm while others in light blue stand behind her, showing a Saturday crowd shot from a noon kickoff in Oxford.

The shot came two plays before Chambliss hit Caleb Cunningham for a six-yard touchdown, and Ole Miss was already up 24-15. The Rebels were close to putting it away, and the broadcast was cutting to the stands instead of the field.

TV directors constantly look for these crowd shots to keep fans engaged during stoppages. For major networks like ABC and ESPN, panning to reactions in the stands is a standard broadcast trick to build atmosphere, especially when a game feels like a blowout or momentum slows down. But when a camera zeroes in on the same fan profile game after game, social media turns a routine production cut into a trending topic.

Auburn had cut it to 17-15 on a Byrum Brown touchdown run, and Alex Golesh went for two and missed. Chambliss answered with a 26-yard touchdown run late in the third. Shekai Mills-Knight opened the fourth with a 10-yard run. Chambliss got a first down with his legs, and the drive covered 72 yards in 11 plays. Cunningham's score made it 31-15 with 12:33 left.

"So they came back in the second half and responded, but I thought it was a combination of early down success in the run game to get them behind the chains and then more importantly, the efficiency of us on offense," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said, according to Evelyn Van Pelt of RebelWalk.

"And I think they felt like, look, man, if we don't extend the drive and we don't score points, like their offense is going to score, and I think they get a little pass happy. So I think they threw it a lot more than the anticipation coming into it."

It did not look like that early. It was 14-9 at halftime, as Chambliss threw a first-half pick to AnQuon Fegans, and an Auburn extra point got blocked. After Cunningham's score, the Rebels hit a 28-yard touchdown pass to Horatio Fields and a 17-yard touchdown run from backup Deuce Knight, who was facing his former team.

Ole Miss scored the final 28 points, outgained Auburn 487-312 and rushed for 224 yards to Auburn's 63. The Rebels were 13-for-16 on third down. Chambliss finished 22-of-34 for 263 yards and two touchdowns, with 65 rushing yards and another score.

Mills-Knight got 16 carries for 71 yards with Kewan Lacy out, and he had 12 career carries coming in. Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) has won 16 straight at home and three in a row over Auburn (4-4, 2-4). The Tigers host Arkansas next.

Georgia comes to Oxford next Saturday on November 7. If the camera finds another fan in the stands against a top-three Georgia team, the internet will notice before the Rebels do.

articles.title: “Turnover Machine” “Sam Leavitt is Already Better”: Fans React as Ole Miss QB Ties LSU Star For Most INTs in SEC 2026 After Crucial Error
articles.summary: Week 9 of the 2026 regular college football season sees the Ole Miss Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC) take on the Auburn Tigers (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadi...
articles.body:
Week 9 of the 2026 regular college football season sees the Ole Miss Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC) take on the Auburn Tigers (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi, on Saturday.

As the first quarter ended scoreless, the pressure to get points on the board was intense heading into the second quarter. As the Ole Miss Rebels led the Auburn Tigers 7-6 with a little over seven minutes left in the second quarter, star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss threw a pass to teammate Deuce Alexander, but the wide receiver dropped it, resulting in a turnover.

For Chambliss, this play added to his interception total this season.

With this interception, Chambliss has now accumulated eight interceptions and is at par with his LSU counterpart, quarterback Sam Leavitt, whom the college football world often compares him to. Both Leavitt and Chambliss are now tied for the most interceptions thrown by a quarterback in the SEC so far this season.

This infamous statistic for Chambliss has prompted fans online to call out his on-field display.

"This Trinidad Chambliss guy is a turnover MACHINE", wrote a fan on X.

"(Sam) Leavitt is already better than Chambliss if you were wondering", commented a fan on X.

At the time of writing, the Ole Miss Rebels lead the Auburn Tigers 24-15 late in the third quarter.

Which Quarterback Has the Most Interceptions in CFB 2026?

While the 2026 college football season has seen amazing moments on the field driven by quarterbacks, it has also seen plenty of misdirected passes and receiver fumbles that have led to more interceptions.

On a list no quarterback wants to top, Akron Zips quarterback Brayden Roggow leads with nine interceptions.

With Roggow leading this dreaded list, seven signal callers have thrown eight interceptions in the first nine weeks of this college football campaign, namely Ashton Daniels (Florida State Seminoles), Marcel Reed (Texas A&M Aggies), Sam Leavitt (LSU Tigers), JJ Kohl (FIU Panthers), Caden Creel (Jacksonville State Gamecocks), Jared Curtis (Vanderbilt Commodores), and Trinidad Chambliss (Ole Miss Rebels).

articles.title: Nets rule out Mikel Brown Jr. vs. Pacers during front end of back-to-back
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets will be without rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr. during Sunday’s road matchup with the Indiana Pacers. They ruled out the No. 6 pick for...
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets will be without rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr. during Sunday's road matchup with the Indiana Pacers . They ruled out the No. 6 pick for the front end of a back-to-back due to back injury management. Brown is expected to play on Monday against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

Brown has come off the bench for the Nets to start this season while on a minutes restriction. He won't play in back-to-backs until that restriction is lifted, which won't happen anytime soon, according to head coach Jordi Fernandez.

"Right now, we're building him up, and if you look at the schedule, we have two days in between [games]. So when you play this amount of minutes, you get assessed. Assessed is how you feel, everything," head coach Jordi Fernandez said after Brown played a season-high 28 minutes during Tuesday's loss to the Boston Celtics. "Then you have 48 hours, and then you play another game. And when he does it for the weeks that we have planned, which I'm not going to share with you guys, and we feel like he's strong enough and he's gone through it and that his body can assimilate all the load, [then he'll be off the minutes limit]. This was one game. He played more because we're confident that with the rest he has [upcoming]. So that's where we are. And right now it's the fourth game. [Mikel won't be off the limit] anytime soon because I want to load him with minutes and have him feeling good."

Brown scored 17 points during the fourth quarter and overtime during his season-high 28 minutes in Boston on Tuesday. He struggled to replicate that production while playing 23 minutes during Friday's 110-94 home loss to the Detroit Pistons.

Nets rule Mikel Brown Jr. out for Pacers matchup on front end of back-to-back

Brown posted 10 points on 2-of-9 shooting from the field and 0-of-4 from three with four assists and two turnovers against Detroit. With Brown sidelined in Indiana, sophomore point guard Nolan Traore will shoulder the bulk of the Nets' ball-handling responsibilities. The French floor general moved into Brooklyn's starting lineup in place of veteran Keon Ellis during the last two games. Traore has averaged 9.4 points, 1.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.0 turnovers on .432/.300/.706 shooting splits in 19.0 minutes per game across five appearances this season.

Despite Brown and Egor Demin (right leg bone bruise) missing Sunday's matchup, the Nets ruled out sophomore point guard Ben Saraf due to a G League assignment. Saraf has been out of Brooklyn's rotation to start this season.

That could open a spot for veteran guard Terance Mann in the Nets' rotation on Sunday. Despite starting 51 games last season, Mann has not been in Brooklyn's rotation this year. The 30-year-old played his first minutes of the season during the fourth quarter of Friday's blowout loss to the Pistons.

Mann averaged 7.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.1 turnovers on .457/.364/.788 shooting splits in 24.3 minutes per game last season. He posted a +4.7 net rating swing (team points scored minus team points allowed per 100 possessions with a player on vs. off), the fourth-best mark on the team.

A top-two team has fallen to an unranked opponent for the fourth consecutive week, and on Saturday, it was Ohio State football 's turn to suffer an unexpected defeat. Ryan Day's team was beaten by USC in its first game without starting quarterback Julian Sayin, and Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy wasted no time expressing his satisfaction with the Buckeyes' disappointing performance.

After Ohio State's loss, Portnoy took to X to openly criticize Day and his team for failing to deliver in crucial matchups.

"It makes me sick to my stomach watching USC bully and bruise a once proud Ohio State team," Portnoy wrote. "Ryan Day once again totally lost when the pressure is on. YOU HATE TO SEE IT! One day Ohio State fans will thank me for bringing Ryan Day's big game ineptitude to justice."

True freshman quarterback Luke Fahey's efforts were not enough to prevent Ohio State from suffering a 30-18 loss against USC, even as Jeremiah Smith delivered another record-breaking performance .

However, the result was particularly unexpected considering USC's recent struggles. Lincoln Riley's team appeared to be in serious trouble after suffering a disappointing blowout loss to Wisconsin the previous week.

Portnoy extended his criticism in the video shared with the post, questioning both USC's overall quality and Riley's coaching ability. Despite

"I'm gonna tell you, this USC team, they're not very good," he said. "Lincoln Riley, soft as a marshmallow. They don't have a top-five win since he's been there, and they just steamroll you guys. They embarrass you guys."

Despite securing the victory, USC was actually outgained by Ohio State in the game. The Buckeyes finished with 464 total yards, including 260 passing yards and 204 rushing yards, compared to USC's 338 total yards, with 222 coming through the air and 116 on the ground.

Ohio State also recorded 25 first downs, significantly more than USC's 15. However, the Trojans made their scoring opportunities count, particularly in the red zone, while their defense prevented the Buckeyes from finding the end zone until the final minutes of the fourth quarter.

articles.title: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream to capture first WNBA crown
articles.summary: Gabby Williams, named Most Valuable Player, sets records for most points (137) and most steals (18) in the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
In a near-single-handed performance, Gabby Williams helped the Golden ⁠⁠State Valkyries defeat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in game seven of the Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA) Finals to give the West Coast franchise a championship in the second year of its existence.

Williams scored 28 of her game-high 30 ‌‌points in the second half to force a turnaround and bag the Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP) award in San Francisco, California, on Saturday.

Kiah Stokes converted a Williams miss into a key hoop with 53 ⁠⁠seconds left to the deafening cheers of “Ballhalla”, as the Valkyries’ home crowd is known at the Chase Center.

In what was mostly a defensive struggle, Williams made the difference in the end, including winning a jump ball over Allisha Gray with 8.3 seconds to go.

With the likes of former San Francisco Giants ⁠⁠superstar Barry Bonds and multiple NBA title-winner Draymond Green of the Golden State Warriors rooting her on, Veronica Burton was fouled with 5.1 seconds remaining and produced the final points in the Valkyries’ storybook season.

On a night when the WNBA had its first game seven in a championship final series, strength in numbers was credited with propelling the second-year franchise to historic heights.

From owner Joe Lacob to coach Natalie Nakase and MVP Williams, one number stood out: 18,064.

“Ballhalla,” Lacob screamed into a microphone in tribute to the capacity crowd during the trophy ceremony.

Williams overcame a two-point first half to become the first player in WNBA postseason history to score 28 points in a half.

The Valkyries’ only All-Star, who was added as a free agent in the offseason, joined Lacob in thanking a crowd that has sold out every game in franchise history, setting league attendance records.

“Honestly, everyone here, not just the players and the staff. [Also] the community, the city, the [San Francisco] Bay [Area],” she gushed on court shortly after having been named the MVP.

“Y’all have been pouring into me all season. It’s a long season and y’all gave me energy.

“When the energy is this good and positive, it’s easy to come to work every day. That’s what I came here for.”

Playing 38 of the game’s 40 minutes, Williams saved enough energy to do a Stephen Curry impersonation on a go-ahead three-pointer with two minutes and 18 seconds (2:18) to go and later win a key jump ball, and Kiah Stokes converted a rare Williams late miss into a key hoop with 53 seconds left, sending the violet-clad crowd into a frenzy.

In the end, Nakase recognised the enormity of piecing together a bunch of players left unprotected in the expansion draft, a handful of international imports and one key free-agent signing into the league’s second-best regular-season record and a victory in the first-ever game seven in WNBA history.

“This is for all the people out there who are underrated, misunderstood. This is for all y’all,” she insisted from midcourt to her home fans and a national television audience as well. “This is proof: If you put all your heart and all your soul [into it], you can win championships.”

Rallying from a nine-point deficit in the third quarter, the Valkyries were tied at 53-all midway through the fourth after Gray connected on a short jumper for Atlanta with 5:14 to play.

Williams, after spearheading an earlier rally, came alive again. She hit two free throws with 3:34 to go and a driving hoop 32 seconds later as the teams exchanged baskets. She then buried arguably the most important shot in Valkyries’ history — a 31-footer to give Golden State the lead for good at 60-57 with 2:18 to go.

She added two free throws, and when Stokes tipped in her teammate’s miss in the final minute, Chase Center erupted as Golden State had a 64-57 advantage that it was able to protect through the end.

“We didn’t let anyone put a limit on us all year,” demanded Burton, who backed Williams with 10 points, 10 rebounds and five assists. “When you work hard, and you put your head down and drive, anything’s possible.”

Williams’s 30 points were her second-most in a playoff game, topped only by the 36 she had in game two of Golden State’s first-round series win over the Dallas Wings on September 30. She made 10 of her 23 field-goal attempts on Saturday when neither team shot well.

She set records for most points (137) and most steals (18) in a WNBA Finals. She also found time for four of Golden State’s eight blocks in the championship game.

Besides holding Dream star Angel Reese to eight points, Stokes had a game-high 13 rebounds for the Valkyries, who won despite making just five of their 20 three-point shots. The Golden State centre also had two blocks, giving her a WNBA Finals-record 19 en route to her fourth title.

Tiffany Hayes also aided the Golden State cause with 11 points.

Jordin Canada had 18 points and Gray 16 for Atlanta, which shot just 33.3 percent overall (23 of 69) and went 6-for-30 from beyond the arc.

“I’m just grateful I got to go to war with this group,” Reese, who led Atlanta with 12 rebounds, assured the media afterwards. “It’s tough in the moment, but we’ll be back.”

Dream coach Karl Smesko lamented what he called “a lot of little stretches” of subpar play, including a game-opening 5:19 in which Atlanta went scoreless, falling behind 8-0 while missing eight straight shots — four three-pointers and four shots from inside the arc that were all blocked — and tossing in four turnovers.

“It’s beyond frustrating that we didn’t accomplish what we set out to accomplish,” he admitted at his postgame news conference. “Those first five minutes … you can’t get those five minutes back.”

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez defeats Christian Mbilli to reclaim WBC title in Riyadh
articles.summary: Mexican boxing star wins 12-round decision to defeat the French fighter and regain the super middleweight belt.
articles.body:
Mexican veteran Saul “Canelo” Alvarez has delivered a commanding performance to defeat French fighter Christian Mbilli and regain his WBC super middleweight title in an emotional victory in Saudi Arabia.

Alvarez won a 12-round decision on Sunday in Riyadh after exerting his influence in the second half of a fight that went ahead despite the escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis.

The 36-year-old Mexican was returning to the ring for the first time since he was beaten by American Terence Crawford in September 2025 in a loss that ended Alvarez’s reign as holder of the division’s four major titles.

He faced Mbilli, 31, who was elevated to titleholder in January, and the fight, which started off as a tight contest, turned into a convincing victory for Alvarez.

The judges scored the contest 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in Alvarez’s favour.

The Mexican superstar struggled for words after receiving the belt.

“It’s so difficult to explain. It’s so difficult to explain,” Alvarez said in English. “It’s something unbelievable. It feels like my first title, now, after 20, 21 years as a professional. Sixteen years ago, I won my first title. Now I won the title again.”

Alvarez added another world title to a haul that stretches from light middleweight to light heavyweight in a 20-year career.

A host of other sporting events has been called off since the Houthis launched drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition that supports Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its fight against the Houthis.

Alvarez hinted at the security situation when he thanked his family “who are watching me from afar today for the first time”.

He was the more composed boxer in the opening round in Riyadh, but by round three, Mbilli was ripping off combinations and looking the more active of the two fighters.

The Frenchman took the initiative in round five although the bout remained a tactical battle.

Alvarez began showing his class and ringcraft in the sixth, easily winning the round, but it was in the seventh that he really pressed home his advantage, pinning Mbilli to the ropes and delivering a right uppercut that had the Frenchman rocking on his feet.

In the eighth, Mbilli had a point taken away for punching behind the head, and he seemed to lose more momentum from then on, allowing Alvarez to begin dictating the fight in the next round as the wily veteran pulled ahead of his younger opponent.

articles.title: Por qué los taxis de Nueva York son amarillos y desde cuándo usan ese color
articles.standfirst: Detrás del color amarillo de los taxis hay una historia que comenzó en hace más de un siglo y que terminó convirtiéndose en un símbolo de la ciudad
articles.summary: Detrás del color amarillo de los taxis hay una historia que comenzó en 1915 y que terminó convirtiéndose en un símbolo de la ciudad
articles.body: Resulta difícil imaginar Nueva York sin sus taxis amarillos. Aparecen en las películas, en las fotografías de Manhattan y en prácticamente cualquier representación de la ciudad. Sin embargo, detrás de ese color tan reconocible hay una historia que comienza mucho antes de que se convirtiera en una de las imágenes más universales del transporte urbano. Una historia en la que intervienen un empresario, un estudio sobre visibilidad y una decisión administrativa que terminó cambiando la imagen de los taxis. Para encontrar uno de los primeros antecedentes hay que remontarse a 1883. Por entonces, la New-York Cab Company decidió pintar de amarillo sus carruajes para diferenciarlos de los de sus competidores. La iniciativa tuvo tanto éxito que otras empresas empezaron a imitarla. El amarillo ya comenzaba a abrirse camino como un color asociado al transporte de pasajeros en la ciudad, aunque todavía faltaban varias décadas para que se convirtiera en una norma. El siguiente paso llegó en 1915, pero no en Nueva York, sino en Chicago. John D. Hertz, empresario que acabaría dando nombre a una de las mayores emrpesas de alquiler de automóviles del mundo, fundó Yellow Cab Company. Su elección del amarillo respondía a una cuestión bastante práctica: quería que sus vehículos pudieran distinguirse fácilmente entre el tráfico. La explicación más extendida apunta a un estudio de aquella época de la Universidad de Chicago que identificaba el amarillo como uno de los colores más visibles a distancia. Más, teniendo en cuenta que ccasi todos los coches eran negros y destacar en medio de la circulación suponía una ventaja comercial. Así que un taxi que se veía mejor también tenía más posibilidades de captar la atención de un cliente. La fórmula funcionó. La compañía de Hertz creció con rapidez y contribuyó a popularizar el amarillo como color característico de los taxis. La decisión se expandió más allá de Chicago y terminó influyendo en la imagen de este tipo de vehículos en otras ciudades estadounidenses. En Nueva York, sin embargo, durante buena parte del siglo XX los taxis no fueron exclusivamente amarillos. Las diferentes compañías y propietarios utilizaban distintos colores, aunque el amarillo ya tenía una presencia importante en las calles. El verdadero cambio llegó a finales de los años sesenta. La ciudad necesitaba encontrar una manera sencilla de distinguir los taxis oficiales, autorizados para recoger pasajeros directamente en la calle, de los vehículos de transporte privado que trabajaban mediante reservas previas. Más cuando la competencia entre ambos modelos había provocado conflictos por las zonas de recogida. La solución se tomó en 1967 y obligaba a los taxis oficiales con licencia municipal a utilizar el amarillo. A partir de entonces, cualquier persona podía reconocer un taxi oficial a simple vista, sin necesidad de comprobar el nombre de la compañía o buscar distintivos específicos. Así, el color se transformó en una herramienta de identificación, una forma de ordenar el transporte y, al mismo tiempo, un elemento de confianza para el pasajero. Los taxis neoyorquinos también han evolucionado sin modificar el tono amrillento que los hace reconocibles, que por reglamento sigue siendo el 'Taxi Yellow' (DuPont M6284 o equivalente). Durante décadas, modelos como los Checker se convirtieron en auténticos iconos de las calles de Manhattan. Después llegaron berlinas como el Chevrolet Caprice o el Ford Crown Victoria, y quienes viajen allí en estos tiempos se encontrarán ya con modelos híbridos y eléctricos. Sin embargo, el cambio de tecnología o de fabricante no ha alterado su principal seña de identidad, y hoy un taxi amarillo es un símbolo de Nueva York reconocible en todo el mundo. Cierto es que desde 2012 existen los llamados 'Boro Taxis', pintados de verde manzana para prestar servicio en los distritos exteriores y en el norte de Manhattan. Pero ello no ha quitado que el amarillo sea el color que siempre buscan los neoyorquinos y los turistas cuando necesitan un taxi.

articles.title: F1: Hamilton takes first Ferrari pole; Antonelli starts fourth in Mexico
articles.summary: George Russell is second fastest and Charles Leclerc third while reigning champion Lando Norris qualifies sixth.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has taken his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix with Mercedes’s Kimi Antonelli fourth on the grid for a ground-breaking race likely to make the 20-year-old Formula One’s youngest champion.

Antonelli needs only a ninth-place finish at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday to become Italy’s first champion since 1953. He was fifth fastest in qualifying, admitting he felt tense, but will move up a place due to Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, in fourth, taking a grid drop.

The pole, in a time of one minute 16.514 seconds, was a record-extending 105th of Hamilton’s stellar career. While he has had two sprint poles since he joined Ferrari last year, he has not had one at a regular grand prix since Hungary in July 2023 when he was at Mercedes – a wait of 1,197 days.

“Thank you so much. It has been such a long time coming,” Hamilton said over the team radio on Saturday. “Mega job, guys. I am so grateful for the hard work you guys put in.”

Hamilton becomes oldest pole-sitter since 1982

The pole also made the seven-time world champion at the age of 41 the oldest pole-sitter since American Mario Andretti, at 42, at Monza in Italy in 1982.

Germany’s Michael Schumacher, who retired from Mercedes in 2012 and won five titles with Ferrari from 2000 to 2004, had his first pole for Ferrari at the 1996 San Marino Grand Prix.

“It feels great to be able to reward them with a pole, and to have your first Ferrari pole, I mean, it just takes me back to watching Michael get all those pole positions when he was at Ferrari and all those wins. So it’s very, very special,” Hamilton said.

Mercedes’s George Russell, Antonelli’s closest rival but 123 points behind his teammate with only 100 to be won after this weekend, was second fastest – just 0.009 adrift after taking provisional pole only for Hamilton to beat his time. Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc was third and 0.119 off the pace.

Both Hamilton and Russell would have to win if either of the remaining contenders is to keep Antonelli waiting another week for the inevitable.

“I struggled to get a good feeling from the tyres in Q3. I just didn’t have the most confidence. I was a bit tense, I am not going to lie,” the Italian said. “It was a poor lap, too many mistakes.

“It has not been the easiest weekend. There is talk of what is there, and I am not as relaxed.”

McLaren’s Lando Norris, the reigning champion and last year’s winner in Mexico, qualified sixth with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar seventh.

Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson qualified eighth fastest but had a one-place grid drop for a clash with Verstappen in Friday’s practice.

The New Zealander was then disqualified from the session for a technical breach and sent to the back of the grid. Teammate Arvid Lindblad will start eighth, Alpine’s Pierre Gasly ninth and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg 10th.

“I went to see Max this morning to apologise because what happened doesn’t need to happen and I don’t want it to happen in future,” Lawson said.

Antonelli was only seventh in the second phase with Norris the fastest and teammate Oscar Piastri knocked out in 13th place in a blow for McLaren’s hopes of edging back in front of Red Bull in the battle for third overall.

The Australian complained of a lack of rear grip after being told he was out of the top 10.

Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso halted the first session when the team told him to stop in the stadium section with a suspected water pressure issue in the power unit.

The Spaniard was then noted for a general safety incident after he failed to reattach the steering wheel after getting out of the car.

Hamilton was fastest in that first session with Antonelli only ninth.

Japanese Ryo Hirakawa qualified 19th for Haas as he made his F1 race debut this weekend at the age of 32 and in place of Esteban Ocon, who was dropped by the team for undisclosed reasons not related to illness.

Mexican Sergio Perez, preparing for his 300th grand prix in front of his home crowd and Cadillac teammate Valtteri Bottas filled the back row.

articles.title: BS Meter on New Crown Jewel Match, John Cena Classic Latest, A Seth Rollins Update, More WWE Rumors
articles.summary: A hot week for the pro wrestling rumor mill is inevitable when John Cena comes back to the sport's orbit.
articles.body:
A hot week for the pro wrestling rumor mill is inevitable when John Cena comes back to the sport's orbit.

So it goes this week with Cena on his way back for an appearance. There's a newfound buzz around the so-called upcoming John Cena Classic as the big-ticket item there.

Tack on big upcoming events from WWE and AEW, with the former still heading overseas in some capacity. There's rumblings not only of major plans for certain wrestlers, but even a big backstage shakeup that could impact every single piece of weekly WWE programming.

To help fans keep up with the rumor mill, let's toss the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

Big things happening behind the scenes in WWE, it seems. According to PWInsider (h/t WrestleOps' Harry Smith ), Bruce Prichard is stepping away from his spot as creative writing executive director, with Shawn Michaels stepping into the void it creates.

Talk about a major development while promoting from within. Justified or not, Prichard has been a sour talking point for a chunk of the WWE fanbase. Michaels, on the other hand, has seen mostly nothing but praise since rising to control most of the creative direction of NXT since 2021.

Easiest buy of the week. Michaels was always headed for bigger things if a spot opened up. We'll see if his arrival is enough to alter the feel of bigger weekly programs and who takes his spot in NXT. But the change is expected.

It seems Big Cass and Rusev are closely linked. According to WrestleVotes (h/t Cageside Seats' Geno Mrosko ), Cass currently holds the spot intended for Rusev before injury. And it gets stranger: According to Self Made Pro (h/t Mrosko ), the two will link up and form a stable with Ethan Page once everyone is back.

Ok then. Cass has been propping up others since his return, losing to the likes of Dragon Lee and Je'Von Evans, among others. Pretty much the same story for Rusev before his absence.

Just randomly throwing two or three guys together for a stable is a pretty WWE thing to do. There's nothing wrong with Cass and Rusev being the guys to take losses and prop up others right now, but there is certainly more upside for storytelling if they can create a little faction and get some momentum for themselves, too.

Are there still plans in the works for some big names? According to Cageside Seats' Cain A. Knight , various outlets report that a Gunther vs. Finn Balor match is being locally advertised before the Crown Jewel PLE.

Much of the news cycle before Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia next week has been on where and if it will take place at all. That has, indeed, made it easy to overlook that, as of this writing, there are only four matches planned and some major names like Balor and Gunther haven't been included.

We'll see on this one. What's advertised locally, even around the United States, doesn't always match up with what happens. Plans change, injuries happen, advertising partners aren't informed, etc. We can all agree, at least, that WWE has largely mishandled Gunther since his spree of retiring pro wrestling legends.

Ranking WWE and AEW's Most Overrated Wrestlers

Here's a weird one: Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (h/t Knight ) reported that WWE knew almost right away that the Montez Ford lap dance incident would cause problems and that it might just explain why Seth Rollins hasn't been on weekly programming too.

For those way out of the loop, a guard involved with an on-screen interaction with Ford is suing the wrestler and WWE . Rollins was mostly last seen getting help from The Street Profits in a bit of faction drama before fading to the background again.

Oddity of the whole lawsuit thing aside, it would make some sense if this sudden bit of news has caused a bit of planning chaos around Rollins. There's no reason to rush him off into something else if the off-screen stuff gets settled soon. On the other hand, this is Rollins , and keeping him off television for any reason when healthy is, well, pretty silly.

Ready for more weird John Cena Classic buzz? According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Knight ), there has been "an incredible" number of creative meetings about what to actually do with the new event. It also apparently will now stream on more than one platform after initially being pitched as a Club WWE thing.

So, for those who forgot, Cena announced this new WWE event but offered no details. Buzz suggested it would be a tournament where perhaps wins and losses didn't matter while fans voted on the real winners. Or something. The makings of an interesting, fan-engaging idea were there, but WWE has been radio silent about the whole thing since for good reason.

Kudos to WWE and Cena for not just pretending the whole announcement never happened. At least they still plan to try something. Whether that something turns out to be any good very much remains to be seen. But it sounds like fans could find out more when Cena returns to Raw next week.

articles.title: NHL Trade Block Big Board for November 2026
articles.summary: The first month of the 2026-27 NHL regular season is history, but it also came with a pair of big trades.
articles.body:
The first month of the 2026-27 NHL regular season is history, but it also came with a pair of big trades.

A blockbuster deal occurred just before we published our October NHL Trade Block Big Board , when the Columbus Blue Jackets shipped Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for Matthew Knies. Both had featured in our previous trade boards.

On Oct. 23, a more prominent player from our October board finally moved, as the Winnipeg Jets traded goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner topped every one of our trade boards since July.

Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin has also featured prominently on our trade boards since he went public with his trade request in June. Recent rumors suggest he could be the next noteworthy star to be moved in an early-season blockbuster, which is becoming the norm this season.

At least, that's how it looked until Oct. 30, when it was reported that Tampa Bay Lightning superstar Nikita Kucherov wouldn't sign an extension and had requested a trade.

Larkin is among the few players from our previous board to make it onto our November board. Most have dropped out of the rumor mill as speculation focused on other players throughout October. Meanwhile, Alexander Nikishin was dropped after signing a one-year deal with the Carolina Hurricanes.

Follow along to see which other notable players joined Larkin and Kucherov in the rumor mill over the past month. As always, the players' skills, experience, contracts, and likelihood of being moved factored into our compilation.

Uncertainty over Quinn Hughes' future with the Minnesota Wild earned him a spot on our last two Trade Boards. Wild general manager Bill Guerin said in September that he would give the 27-year-old superstar defenseman all the time he needed to make his decision.

Hughes can become an unrestricted free agent next July and would be among the biggest names in the UFA market. He's in the final season of a six-year contract worth an average annual value of $7.9 million. As an elite NHL defenseman, he could command over $20 million annually on his next contract.

On Oct. 1, Wild beat writers Michael Russo and Joe Smith of The Athletic suggested that Guerin would have to consider moving Hughes by the March 1 trade deadline if he remains unsigned. It would be "the nightmare scenario," considering how much Guerin gave up in future assets to acquire Hughes last season.

Fast-forward to Oct. 27, when Guerin told a local radio station he hadn't held contract talks with Hughes for some time , adding that he wasn't going to try to beg the blueliner to sign. That won't mollify nervous Wild fans or silence the conjecture about his immediate future.

Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski was the subject of trade chatter in late June following reports that he was considering his future. He was reportedly close to being shipped to the Dallas Stars until he and general manager Don Waddell released statements reiterating his commitment to the club.

That silenced the speculation for several months. However, the Blue Jackets' inconsistent performance throughout October prompted Sportsnet's Michael Amato to ponder the effect that another potentially lost season could have on the reigning Norris Trophy winner's future in Columbus.

Werenski is signed through 2027-28 , but the Blue Jackets can open extension talks next July. However, Amato thinks they're running out of time to convince the 29-year-old blueliner to stay in Columbus.

Amato envisioned a scenario where Werenski requests a trade before the March 1 trade deadline. That's a possibility worth considering if the Blue Jackets fail to rise among the playoff contenders this season.

The Philadelphia Flyers' hopes of building on last season's surprising playoff appearance have crashed back to earth following a 3-8-4 record in their first 15 games . That poor start has their followers wondering what general manager Daniel Briere will do to get them back on the winning track.

On Oct. 13, Daily Faceoff's Anthony Di Marco reported that sources claimed some within the organization were frustrated over Konecny's performance. It was suggested the 28-year-old winger could be approached about waiving his no-movement clause if the club failed to improve.

Di Marco followed up a week later, saying the Flyers had to address their logjam of wingers. While Owen Tippett drew the most interest around the league, Di Marco felt that was because of Konecny's NMC, adding that the latter had more value as the better all-around player.

However, Flyers beat writer Kevin Kurz of The Athletic considered it " incredibly unlikely " that Konecny would be traded in the near future, citing his value to the team as well as his contract and no-movement protection. Nevertheless, one can't fully dismiss the possibility given where the Flyers are right now.

The Vancouver Canucks' rebuilding process made earned winger Jake DeBrusk the No. 13 spot on our previous NHL Trade Block Big Board . Given the Canucks' current position at the bottom of the standings , DeBrusk could resurface more frequently in the rumor mill as the season progresses.

DeBrusk, 30, is signed through 2030-31 . He carries an average annual value of $5.5 million, which is now an affordable rate for a top-six winger. This is the final season that he has a full no-movement clause, as it shifts to a 15-team no-trade list next July.

With eight points in 13 games, DeBrusk is off to a decent start to this season. On Oct. 12, Ben Kuzma of The Vancouver Province reported that the veteran winger was working on other aspects of his game, including doing more without the puck and using his speed more effectively on the forecheck.

Kuzma suggested that the improvement in DeBrusk's overall game could bolster his stock in the trade market. That could make him a player to watch as teams start shopping for an experienced scoring winger.

Ivan Miroshnichenko, Washington Capitals

Thanks to offseason additions Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, the Washington Capitals have considerable depth on their wings this season. However, it's also made it difficult for promising Ivan Miroshnichenko to crack the lineup.

Miroshnichenko, 22, was chosen 20th overall by the Capitals in the 2022 NHL Draft. The additions of Tuch and Kyrou, and the emergence of wingers Aliaksei Protas and Ryan Leonard, have limited him to three games this season. He's in the second year of a two-year contract worth an affordable $925,000 annually.

On October 24, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Capitals permitted Miroshnichenko and his agent to speak with other NHL clubs. Four days later, Dave Pagnotta of The Fourth Period claimed the Chicago Blackhawks, Philadelphia Flyers, Calgary Flames, and Seattle Kraken were interested.

Rebuilding teams like Chicago, Philadelphia, and Calgary can give Miroshnichenko more playing time. Meanwhile, the Kraken are on the lookout for players who can help them offensively.

On the eve of the opening night of this regular season, the Columbus Blue Jackets traded Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs for winger Matthew Knies in a blockbuster deal. However, that move did little to improve their fortunes, as their play was inconsistent in October.

Those difficulties sparked speculation that another Blue Jackets winger could be a trade candidate. On Oct. 22, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that some teams had called to express interest in Dmitri Voronkov.

The 26-year-old winger is slated to become a restricted free agent with arbitration rights next summer. He's in the second season of a two-year contract with an average annual value of $4.18 million. The 6'5", 230-pounder is a big, physical forward who had a career high of 23 goals and 24 assists for 47 points in 2024-25.

LeBrun couldn't say if Voronkov would be traded, but he claimed the Blue Jackets were listening. His situation bears watching as November rolls along, especially if the Jackets struggle to gain ground in the standings.

Contract talks between the Detroit Red Wings and Simon Edvinsson took an ominous turn on Oct. 3, when Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported the restricted free-agent defenseman preferred a trade.

It's been frequently reported that Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff's priority is re-signing the 23-year-old Edvinsson. Nevertheless, Horcoff is also reportedly fielding calls from clubs interested in the skillful young blueliner.

TSN's Pierre LeBrun claimed the Sharks and Boston Bruins were among 10 teams pursuing Edvinsson. The Hockey News ' Eric Cruickshank listed the San Jose Sharks, St. Louis Blues, and Toronto Maple Leafs as potential suitors. Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli felt he'd be a good fit with the Philadelphia Flyers.

The 5 pm ET deadline on Dec. 1 for signing restricted free agents hangs over this situation. If Edvinsson remains unsigned by then, he'll be eligible to play in the NHL for the remainder of the season.

articles.title: Ranking WWE and AEW's Most Overrated Wrestlers
articles.summary: Professional wrestling is built on opinions, and few debates get fans arguing faster than whether a performer actually deserves the praise, championships, and main-event opportunities they receive.
articles.body:
Professional wrestling is built on opinions, and few debates get fans arguing faster than whether a performer actually deserves the praise, championships, and main-event opportunities they receive.

Being overrated doesn't necessarily mean someone is bad at their job, but there comes a point when popularity, reputation, or presentation starts doing more of the heavy lifting than the performances themselves.

With that in mind, here are the WWE and AEW Superstars whose standing in the wrestling business deserves a closer look.

There is no denying that Uso knows how to get a crowd on its feet, but getting a reaction and delivering consistently great singles matches are two very different things. Uso's entrance has become one of WWE's most recognizable spectacles, and his popularity has helped him reach heights that once seemed unlikely for a member of a legendary tag team. The question is whether the in-ring performances have consistently justified that level of success.

Uso's greatest strength is his connection with the audience, but his singles offense and match structure can feel limited compared with those of other wrestlers competing for the same spotlight. His biggest moments often rely on the crowd, the entrance, and the emotional buildup rather than a consistently impressive body of work between the ropes.

Punk remains one of professional wrestling's most compelling talkers, and few performers can make a personal rivalry feel as important as he can. His ability to generate interest in a match is undeniable, but his reputation sometimes protects him from the same scrutiny applied to other wrestlers. When the promos end and the bell rings, the performances need to live up to expectations, and Punk has failed.

Punk's age, experience, and injury history are legitimate considerations, but they don't automatically make every match great or feud memorable. His strengths are obvious, yet the overall package doesn't always match his reputation as an elite performer. He can still be a major attraction without being untouchable in discussions about who delivers the best work in WWE.

Rhodes has become one of WWE's defining stars, and his ability to connect with audiences has helped make him a reliable centerpiece for the company. However, being positioned as the face of WWE also means receiving a level of attention and protection that not every performer enjoys. The question is whether his character and matches consistently justify that status.

Rhodes is a polished performer, but his presentation can sometimes feel more compelling than the stories he tells. The familiar persona, entrances, and championship runs can make even an ordinary feud feel tired. He deserves credit for his accomplishments, but that doesn't mean his spot at the top of the card is beyond criticism.

Mercedes Moné arrived in AEW with an enormous reputation, a decorated WWE résumé, and name recognition few wrestlers can match. Those accomplishments established lofty expectations, but a name and an impressive collection of championships don't automatically make every subsequent run a success. AEW needed to turn her star power into compelling television, memorable rivalries, and performances that consistently justified the investment.

Moné is an accomplished wrestler, but her presentation can sometimes lean too heavily on her established reputation instead of making each new rivalry feel essential. When a performer is promoted as one of the biggest names in the industry, the standard should be more than simply being good enough to win matches and collect titles.

Ricochet can do things in the ring that most performers wouldn't even attempt, and his athleticism is his greatest asset. His moves can produce instant highlights, but professional wrestling requires more than an impressive collection of aerial maneuvers. A great performer needs character development, compelling rivalries, and the ability to make the audience emotionally invested in a match.

Ricochet's physical ability has never been the issue; the question is whether his character work and storytelling have consistently reached the same level. A spectacular sequence might earn a reaction, but the moments that surround it are what turn a highlight into a memorable match, and he hasn't shown that ability outside of Lucha Underground.

Callis is an effective wrestling villain, and his ability to generate heat has made him a valuable part of AEW's presentation. He understands how to make himself obnoxious, manipulate situations, and give audiences someone to boo. However, there is a difference between being an effective manager and becoming such a constant presence that the act starts to wear thin.

Callis can help elevate the wrestlers around him, but his involvement can also become a crutch when too many stories revolve around his interference, schemes, and familiar promos. A manager should enhance the talent, not become the primary reason an audience pays attention to a feud. Callis remains useful in his role, but AEW risks diminishing his impact when it relies on the same formula too often, instead of letting the wrestlers carry the stories.

articles.title: No. 1 Florida returns to Tampa with deep feelings from NCAA stunner
articles.summary: GAINESVILLE — Florida coach Todd Golden never really planned to open the season in Tampa, the site of one of the most painful NCAA Tournament losses in progr...
articles.body:
GAINESVILLE — Florida coach Todd Golden never really planned to open the season in Tampa, the site of one of the most painful NCAA Tournament losses in program history.

Nonetheless, facing No. 14 Miami at Benchmark International Arena on Monday night should provide the top-ranked Gators a chance to purge eight months of bitterness.

Winning a second national title in three years would be the ultimate atonement for a stunning 73-72 loss to ninth-seeded Iowa in March — the one that wiped out any shot at winning back-to-back championships.

For now, though, Florida will use a return to Tampa as motivation while essentially trying to pick up where it left off last season and reignite its chase for another crown.

"It's awesome; I love it," guard Urban Klavzar said. "I love going back there, and we're definitely going to have a different result. I don't think we should think too much about (being) in the same city, same arena. I think we should take it as, 'just remember the loss.'"

Florida had a three-point lead and the ball with 1:30 to play. But All-American Thomas Haugh shot an air ball and missed a 3-pointer on one possession. Isaiah Brown missed a free throw on another. And the Gators had a defensive lapse in the final seconds that led to Alvaro Folgueiras' 3-pointer from the corner.

Golden's group had one final chance with 4.5 seconds left. Xaivian Lee drove the length of the court and into the paint before delivering a low pass to Haugh that bounced off his legs as time expired.

Haugh and several Florida teammates were in tears after the final buzzer, which sent the Hawkeyes and their fans into a frenzy. Haugh called it the most distraught he's ever been after a game.

"I may have watched it a couple times, but that was like right after it happened," Haugh said. "That feeling is still deep in our hearts somewhere with everybody that came back, and we're not going to let that happen again. That's why we came back."

Rueben Chinyelu, Alex Condon and Haugh started contemplating a return to Florida a few weeks later. All of them credited that loss as the catalyst for wanting another year — another title shot, really — in college.

Florida made it happen, spending roughly $25 million to bring back four starters and retain nine of its top 11 scorers.

And the setback that defined last season — and set the stage for this one — has been a driving force ever since, whether it was on the court or during 6 a.m. workouts.

"For us to achieve what we want, we have to come out every day and give it our all," Chinyelu said. "And every guy, from the coaches today, last month, they understood that, and every day they bring it up."

Florida and Miami played early last season in Jacksonville and had discussed making it an annual series that moves to other neutral sites around the state. Orlando and Tampa were obvious options.

Tampa made more sense because of how last season ended. Florida State and Florida A&M will play in the first game of a doubleheader.

"It's a great venue," Golden said. "It's been good to us, and we're not going to let one poor performance dictate whether we play there again or not. Just something that everything kind of aligned for us to be back there."

Monday, No. 1 Florida vs. No. 14 Miami, 6 p.m., Florida State vs. Florida A&M, 8:30; Benchmark International Arena. TV: ESPN2. Tickets: Ticketmaster.com. Visit benchmarkintlarena.com or call 813-301-2500 for details.

articles.title: Blockbusters, Glory & Scandal: Novembers That Changed the Astros Forever
articles.summary: November does not belong to baseball, at least not by design. Yet, the Houston Astros time and time again have dominated the headlines throughout one of the...
articles.body:
November does not belong to baseball, at least not by design. Yet, the Houston Astros time and time again have dominated the headlines throughout one of the games quietest months. Today we revisit the November moments that redefined the course of Astros history.

November 1, 2017. Every Astros fan knows the date by heart. Houston was still rebuilding from Harvey and that night, the title meant something far beyond the white lines. The first championship took an astonishing 55 years to claim. 1,830 days later, they'd do it all over again, claiming title number two which validated their dynasty. If you close your eyes, you can see Yordan Alvarez's monster 3-run 450-foot blast in Game 6 vs. the Phillies. November 5, 2022, would be the last, for now.

November 29, 1971. Worst trade in team history.

The Astros sent future hall of famer Joe Morgan to Cincinnati it resulted in the final piece for what would become the Reds potent "Big Red Machine" From the early 70's through 1979, the Reds would average 95 wins a season in route to a pair of World Series. All told, eight different players were part of the deal between the Reds and Astros.

26 years later, the Astros would land a star of their own. November 11th, 1997. Fresh off slugging three home runs in the 1997 World Series for the victorious (then-Florida) Marlins, the Astros acquired Moises Alou. Alou would play three seasons in Houston and was a 2x All-Star thanks largely to his power numbers.

Ken Rosenthal and Evan Drellich publish a report chronicling the electronic sign-stealing system thanks to former teammate, Mike Fiers. That article would set the sports world on its ear, ultimately costing the Astros multiple draft picks, suspensions, firings and a $5 million fine.

Drayton McLane sold the Astros to Jim Crane and set the stage for the franchise's move to the American League. MLB approved the $680 million dollar price tag on this date, ending McLane's 19-year ownership run. Houston would have 14 winning seasons during that 19-year span.

Every November moment speaks for itself. It's where history lives in this city. It's the month that shaped the franchise, and once again, it's back.

articles.title: Despite Their Struggles, the Chargers are Better Off Keeping Mike McDaniel This Season
articles.summary: Despite the Chargers’ offensive struggles, firing Mike McDaniel now may not be the answer. With the season slipping away, Los Angeles should give him the res...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers have reached a point where it is difficult to find many positives about their offense. At 0-6, the season is quickly slipping away, and the team has looked nowhere close to what many expected when Mike McDaniel was hired to lead the offense. Still, despite the struggles, keeping McDaniel in place for the remainder of the season may be the best decision the Chargers can make.

Jim Harbaugh said today that McDaniel will continue calling the offense as the Chargers prepare to return from their bye week. While plenty of fans have been calling for a change, there is a reasonable argument for giving McDaniel more time to figure things out rather than making a midseason switch.

The results have been unacceptable. The Chargers have struggled to score points, Justin Herbert has been turning the ball over far too often and the offense has consistently failed to capitalize on opportunities. Through six games, there has been very little evidence that McDaniel's system is working the way it was supposed to.

However, firing him now would not necessarily solve those problems.

McDaniel has a track record of putting together productive offenses. During his time in Miami, his offenses showed the ability to create explosive plays and put up points. There is a reason the Chargers brought him in to work with Herbert in the first place. The idea was to pair one of the league's most talented quarterbacks with an offensive mind capable of maximizing his abilities.

That has not happened yet, but it is worth finding out whether the two can eventually make it work.

The Chargers have dealt with injuries along the offensive line and at wide receiver, while turnovers, dropped passes and penalties have compounded the issues. Those problems do not excuse the coaching or play-calling, but they are worth considering before deciding that the entire plan needs to be scrapped.

With the season already looking lost, the Chargers have little to gain from making a desperate move simply to show that something is changing. Instead, the priority should be simplifying the offense, getting healthier and finding some consistency over the final stretch of the season.

If McDaniel can get the offense moving in the right direction, even if the wins do not immediately follow, that would give the organization something to build on heading into next year. The Chargers need to see progress from Herbert, establish a more reliable running game and find ways to get their playmakers involved. Those are reasonable goals even with the postseason likely out of reach.

There is also the question of who would replace McDaniel. Adam Gase has experience as an offensive coordinator and could certainly take over the play-calling duties. However, his presence does not automatically make him a better option. His successful work with Peyton Manning in Denver came years ago, and his subsequent head-coaching tenures in Miami and New York left plenty of questions about his ability to lead an offense consistently.

Replacing McDaniel with Gase would be a gamble of its own, not a guaranteed improvement.

The Chargers need accountability, and McDaniel should be judged on what happens from here. Keeping him does not mean giving him a free pass for the team's offensive failures. It means allowing him the opportunity to demonstrate that the ideas that made him an attractive hire can translate to Los Angeles.

At this point, the Chargers should be looking beyond salvaging a disastrous season. They need to determine whether McDaniel can be part of the solution moving forward. If the offense continues to look this bad over the coming weeks, difficult decisions will be unavoidable.

For now, though, giving McDaniel the rest of the season to prove himself makes more sense than starting over in October. The Chargers have already lost plenty of time. They might as well use the remaining games to find out whether this offense has a future.

articles.title: Oregon men's basketball resets with new coach and roster
articles.summary: Oregon men's basketball begins a new era under interim coach Tony Stubblefield with a roster full of new faces.
articles.body:
A new coach and nearly a dozen new players offer a fresh start for an Oregon men's basketball program coming off its worst season in nearly 20 years.

The Ducks will tip off their 32-game regular season Nov. 2 with a 7 p.m. nonconference game against Montana at Matthew Knight Arena, and they will look almost unrecognizable when they do so.

Longtime assistant Tony Stubblefield has moved into the interim-head coach position following the retirement of Dana Altman, who abruptly ended his 16-year career at Oregon on Oct. 7 .

Oregon men's basketball resets with new coach and roster

Stubbledfield takes command of a roster that includes nine transfers, two freshmen and just two scholarship players returning from last season's team that went 12-20.

So, what should fans expect this season from a team that is still very much learning how to play with each other and for a coach who has assumed his position?

"Our guys are making progress," Stubblefield said Friday. "It takes time but this group has been very coachable. It's a really good group of guys."

With so many new players and unfamiliar faces, here's a refresher on who is on the team heading into the opener.

Jerry Easter II, 6-4, sophomore: A transfer from USC who started seven games for the Trojans and averaged 4.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, 1.1 assists.

Jasper Johnson, 6-5, sophomore: The transfer from Kentucky averaged 4.9 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 35 games for the Wildcats. He was a five-star prospect in the 2025 recruiting class.

Fred Payne, 6-2, senior: The transfer point guard from Boston College started 30 games last season and averaged a team-high 15.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.1 steals.

Tyrone Riley IV, 6-6, junior: A 65-game starter for San Francisco the last two seasons. As a sophomore in 2025-26 he averaged 12.2 points, 4.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.0 steals and named all-WCC second-team.

Wei Lin, 6-4, junior: The reserve guard played in 30 games with nine starts last season for the Ducks. He averaged 6.6 points and 1.7 assists.

Tajh Ariza, 6-9, freshman: A five-star prospect and the No. 32 ranked player in the 2026 recruiting class by 247Sports.

Dwayne Aristode, 6-8, sophomore: The transfer from Arizona played in 35 games and averaged 3.8 points and 1.7 rebounds.

Taylor Bol Bowen, 6-10, senior: The transfer from Alabama played in 30 games with 11 starts last season and averaged 6.3 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.0 blocks.

Andrew Meadow, 6-6, senior: Started 68 games in three seasons at Boise State, including 32 last season when he averaged 12.1 points, 3.6 rebounds and shot 51% from the field and 38.6% from 3-point range.

Pharaoh Compton, 6-7, junior: The transfer from San Diego State averaged 7.5 points and 2.8 rebounds last season.

Seven Spurlock, 6-5, freshman: The first-year player from Dallas was a three-star recruit.

Sean Stewart, 6-9, senior: The returning post played in 32 games and made 23 starts for the Ducks last season. He averaged 6.5 points and 5.2 rebounds.

Malique Ewin, 6-10, fifth year: The transfer from Arkansas played in 37 games last season with four starts, including all three of the Razorbacks' NCAA Tournament games. He averaged 9.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.1 blocks and 1.0 assists and shot 59% from the field.

What will Oregon's starting lineup look like against Montana?

The Ducks played three exhibition games in October and went 1-2, though they were noticeably more cohesive and in sync in game three – a win against Stanford – than they were in game one – a loss to Seattle.

Meadow was the only player to start all three games. Guards Payne, Riley and Johnson started two games, with each getting one start with the other two players.

Stewart and Aristode also made two starts, and Compton and Bol Bowen started once each.

Stubblefield wasn't ready to announce a starting lineup for the season opener.

"It's really hard to say," Stubblefield said. "Our strength is really indeed in numbers. We have depth, and again, it changes on a day-to-day basis. … I don't necessarily say we have a best five. We have a really, really good team that is a very deep team."

articles.title: Fifa Laopakdee headed back to Masters, Open at St. Andrews with repeat Asia-Pacific Am win
articles.summary: Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand became the second player to win back-to-back in the Asia-Pacific Amateur with another Sunday comeback.
articles.body:
TOMARATA, New Zealand — Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand became the second player to win back-to-back in the Asia-Pacific Amateur with another Sunday comeback, this time without having to win in a playoff. He closed with a 1-under 70 for a three-shot victory.

That sends Laopakdee back to Augusta National in April for the Masters, along with a return trip to The Open next summer at St. Andrews.

The 21-year-old Thai said he exchanged phone numbers at the last Masters with Justin Rose, who promised him a practice round if Laopakdee made it back.

"Rosey, see you at a practice round for the Masters," Laopakdee said with a wide smile.

Laopakdee, three shots behind with 10 holes to play at Te Arai Links, flipped the script in one hole when he hit his approach just over the false front to 7 feet for a birdie on No. 11, and Zack Swanwick of New Zealand shockingly took a triple bogey.

That four-shot swing took Laopakdee form a two-shot deficit to a two-shot lead, and the Arizona State senior didn't give Swanwick much of a chance to catch him.

Laopakdee effectively ended it with a wedge to 4 feet on the par-3 17th for one final birdie, stretching his lead to four shots. Swanwick, who began the final round with a two-shot lead over Laopakdee and Cooper Moore, didn't make a birdie until the par-5 closing hole. He shot 75.

Laopakdee joined Masters champion Hideki Matsuyama as the only players to win consecutive years since the Asia-Pacific Amateur began in 2009.

He repeatedly shook his fists when he tapped in for par on the 18th to finish at 6-under 278 at the wind-blown seaside course about an hour north of Auckland.

It was a tough ending for Swanwick, trying to become the first Kiwi to win the Asia-Pacific Amateur in front of a home crowd, in a year when New Zealand celebrated another major champion in Ryan Fox at Royal Birkdale.

Swanwick, a junior at Florida, had a two-shot lead going to the 11th hole when his 6-iron was a little strong and went into a back bunker. His shot came out a fraction too strong, rolled past the pin and then off the false front into a deep swale. His chip-and-run up the slope came back to his feet. The next chip barely stayed on the green and he missed then 8-foot putt to take triple bogey.

"Middle of the green, make par and get out of there," Swanwick said. "I hit into the bunker, just flew the bunker shot a little too far and got a little too cute with the chip. Just had a few mistakes that cost me."

Swanwick looked he might get it back on the par-5 13th into the wind. His second shot came up short and he pitched to 10 feet for a chance at birdie. Laopakdee drove into a sandy area, and only advanced the ball some 40 yards into more sand. He laid up, then hit wedge to 20 feet.

Laopakdee rolled in the long par putt, and Swanwick missed his birdie. Instead of a chance to tie for the lead, the Kiwi was still two behind. And on the short par-4 14th, Swanwick drilled driver onto the green, some 70 feet away. He rolled a putt over the ridge to about 8 feet, missed the birdie putt and the missed the 4-foot par putt. The four-putt bogey sent him three behind.

"It was tough luck for Zack on 11, it was super windy," Laopakdee said. "I somehow hit a great second shot and made birdie and it created huge momentum for me."

Kayun Mudadana of Australia closed with a 67 and finished alone in third at 2-under 282. Moore birdied the last hole for 75 and was another shot back. Only four players finished under par.

A year ago in Dubai, Laopakdee rallied from a six-shot deficit in the final round and won the Asia-Pacific on the third playoff hole.

Laopakdee, at No. 31 in the world amateur ranking, won the Desimone Invitational in early March at Lake Merced in San Francisco. But the rest of the year was a disappointment until Sunday.

"This is one of the last events of the year, and I wanted to prove to myself that I've still got it," he said. "To pull it off, it means the whole world to me."

While he was able to take part in the Chiefs' workouts on Wednesday, a shoulder injury kept Delane from participating in practices on Thursday and Friday.

Delane has officially been ruled out for Kansas City's rivalry matchup against Denver in Week 8. It is unclear how many more games the former LSU Tiger might have to miss as he tends to his shoulder injury.

Up-and-coming defensive backs Nohl Williams and Jadon Canady will get extra playing time in Week 8 as Delane continues his recovery.
